questions.question: Define finite, renewable and sustainable resources, and explain why renewable does not automatically mean impact-free.
questions.modelAnswer: Finite used faster than formed; renewable replenished on human timescale; sustainable meets present needs without compromising future needs. Renewable extraction/land/energy/ecosystem impacts remain and rate of use must not exceed replacement.
markingPoints: Finite used faster than formed
renewable replenished on human timescale
sustainable meets present needs without compromising future needs. Renewable extraction/land/energy/ecosystem impacts remain and rate of use must not exceed replacement.

questions.question: Describe treatment of freshwater to make potable water and explain why potable does not mean pure.
questions.modelAnswer: Choose source; sedimentation/filtration remove solids; sterilise by chlorine/ozone/UV to kill microbes; test/adjust. Potable has safe levels of dissolved substances/microbes but contains minerals.
markingPoints: Choose source
sedimentation/filtration remove solids
sterilise by chlorine/ozone/UV to kill microbes
test/adjust. Potable has safe levels of dissolved substances/microbes but contains minerals.

questions.question: Compare distillation and reverse osmosis for desalination, including mechanism, energy/cost and environmental issue.
questions.modelAnswer: Distillation evaporates/condenses; high heat energy. RO high pressure through membrane; electrical energy/membrane. Both costly; concentrated brine/ecosystem and carbon impacts; suitability depends on energy/water scarcity.
markingPoints: Distillation evaporates/condenses
high heat energy. RO high pressure through membrane
electrical energy/membrane. Both costly
concentrated brine/ecosystem and carbon impacts
suitability depends on energy/water scarcity.

questions.question: Describe sewage treatment from screening to discharge, including sludge and effluent pathways.
questions.modelAnswer: Screen grit/large objects; sedimentation separates sludge/effluent; anaerobic digestion of sludge produces biogas; aerobic microbes treat effluent/organic matter; discharge after treatment; industrial toxins may need removal.
markingPoints: Screen grit/large objects
sedimentation separates sludge/effluent
anaerobic digestion of sludge produces biogas
aerobic microbes treat effluent/organic matter
discharge after treatment
industrial toxins may need removal.

questions.question: Design the AQA water-analysis and purification practical, including pH, dissolved solids, distillation and safety.
questions.modelAnswer: Measure pH consistently; evaporate known volume in preweighed dish, dry/cool/reweigh for solids; distil with anti-bumping, condenser water flow, collect distillate; eye protection/heat care; repeats, same volumes, avoid contamination.
markingPoints: Measure pH consistently
evaporate known volume in preweighed dish, dry/cool/reweigh for solids
distil with anti-bumping, condenser water flow, collect distillate
eye protection/heat care
repeats, same volumes, avoid contamination.

questions.question: A dish is 42.36 g empty and 42.61 g after evaporating 50.0 cm3 water. Calculate dissolved-solids concentration in g/dm3.
questions.modelAnswer: Solids=0.25 g; volume=0.0500 dm3; concentration=0.25/0.0500=5.0 g/dm3.
markingPoints: Solids=0.25 g
volume=0.0500 dm3
concentration=0.25/0.0500=5.0 g/dm3.

questions.question: Explain the four main LCA stages and why two published LCAs of the same product may disagree.
questions.modelAnswer: Raw extraction/processing; manufacture/packaging; use; disposal/end of life. Different boundaries, data, assumptions, transport, electricity mix, number of reuses and subjective weighting/omissions.
markingPoints: Raw extraction/processing
manufacture/packaging
use
disposal/end of life. Different boundaries, data, assumptions, transport, electricity mix, number of reuses and subjective weighting/omissions.

questions.question: A reusable bottle causes five times the manufacture impact of a disposable bottle but one-fifth the impact per wash/use after manufacture. Explain how to determine the break-even number of uses and what extra data are needed.
questions.modelAnswer: Set total impacts equal: manufacture + n(use/end impacts); solve using actual numerical values. Need disposal, washing energy/water, transport, loss/replacement and recycling rates; relative statement alone may be insufficient for exact n.
markingPoints: Set total impacts equal: manufacture + n(use/end impacts)
solve using actual numerical values. Need disposal, washing energy/water, transport, loss/replacement and recycling rates
relative statement alone may be insufficient for exact n.

questions.question: Compare reducing, reusing and recycling aluminium cans using energy, raw materials, transport and material quality.
questions.modelAnswer: Reduce avoids production; reuse avoids remelting but cleaning/transport/design; recycle saves ore and usually energy but collection/sorting/remelting needed. Aluminium recyclable with little quality loss; balanced context conclusion.
markingPoints: Reduce avoids production
reuse avoids remelting but cleaning/transport/design
recycle saves ore and usually energy but collection/sorting/remelting needed. Aluminium recyclable with little quality loss
balanced context conclusion.

questions.question: Explain rusting requirements and evaluate painting, galvanising and sacrificial protection when a coating is scratched.
questions.modelAnswer: Rust needs O2+water. Paint barrier fails at scratch. Galvanising zinc barrier and zinc oxidises preferentially if scratched. Sacrificial metal must be more reactive and replaced; choose for environment/cost.
markingPoints: Rust needs O2+water. Paint barrier fails at scratch. Galvanising zinc barrier and zinc oxidises preferentially if scratched. Sacrificial metal must be more reactive and replaced
choose for environment/cost.

questions.question: Explain why alloys are often harder than pure metals and select between ceramic, polymer and composite for a bicycle component.
questions.modelAnswer: Different-sized alloy atoms distort layers and stop sliding. Selection must use stated property: ceramic hard/heat-resistant but brittle; polymer light/flexible but may soften; composite high strength-to-mass/designable but costly/recycling difficult.
markingPoints: Different-sized alloy atoms distort layers and stop sliding. Selection must use stated property: ceramic hard/heat-resistant but brittle
polymer light/flexible but may soften
composite high strength-to-mass/designable but costly/recycling difficult.

questions.question: For N2+3H2<=>2NH3, explain the Haber conditions and the function of the iron catalyst.
questions.modelAnswer: ~450 C compromise: lower favours exothermic yield, higher rate. ~200 atm: favours fewer gas moles and rate but costly/risky. Iron lowers activation energy/speeds both directions, reaches equilibrium sooner, no yield-position change. Unreacted gases recycled.
markingPoints: ~450 C compromise: lower favours exothermic yield, higher rate. ~200 atm: favours fewer gas moles and rate but costly/risky. Iron lowers activation energy/speeds both directions, reaches equilibrium sooner, no yield-position change. Unreacted gases recycled.

questions.question: Explain how ammonia is converted into useful fertilisers and why NPK fertilisers are formulations.
questions.modelAnswer: Ammonia reacts with acids to make ammonium salts; nitric acid gives ammonium nitrate; phosphorus/potassium compounds added. NPK contains measured proportions of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium compounds for plant needs.
markingPoints: Ammonia reacts with acids to make ammonium salts
nitric acid gives ammonium nitrate
phosphorus/potassium compounds added. NPK contains measured proportions of nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium compounds for plant needs.

questions.question: Compare phytomining and bioleaching for low-grade copper ores and state how copper can be recovered from the resulting material.
questions.modelAnswer: Plants absorb ions then harvested/burned, metal from ash; bacteria produce leachate. Lower-grade/less landscape damage and energy than conventional mining but slow/land/process issues. Recover by displacement with iron or electrolysis; purity differs.
markingPoints: Plants absorb ions then harvested/burned, metal from ash
bacteria produce leachate. Lower-grade/less landscape damage and energy than conventional mining but slow/land/process issues. Recover by displacement with iron or electrolysis
purity differs.

questions.question: Evaluate replacing a metal car panel with a carbon-fibre composite using a life-cycle approach.
questions.modelAnswer: Compare raw materials, manufacture energy/emissions, mass/fuel savings during use, durability/repair, transport, recyclability/end of life and cost. Lighter use phase may offset high manufacture; conclusion depends on lifetime, energy mix and reuse/recycling data.
markingPoints: Compare raw materials, manufacture energy/emissions, mass/fuel savings during use, durability/repair, transport, recyclability/end of life and cost. Lighter use phase may offset high manufacture
conclusion depends on lifetime, energy mix and reuse/recycling data.

questions.question: What is sustainable development?
questions.modelAnswer: Meeting the needs of current generations without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.
markingPoints: Meeting the needs of current generations without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their needs.

questions.question: Why is most potable water in the UK obtained from fresh water rather than seawater?
questions.modelAnswer: Fresh water needs less treatment and far less energy than desalination, so it is usually cheaper.
markingPoints: Fresh water needs less treatment and far less energy than desalination, so it is usually cheaper.

questions.question: State the main stages used to produce potable water from fresh water.
questions.modelAnswer: Choose a suitable source; pass through filter beds to remove solids; sterilise using chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light.
markingPoints: Choose a suitable source
pass through filter beds to remove solids
sterilise using chlorine, ozone or ultraviolet light.

questions.question: What is the purpose of screening and grit removal during sewage treatment?
questions.modelAnswer: To remove large objects and solid grit before later treatment stages.
markingPoints: To remove large objects and solid grit before later treatment stages.

questions.question: What happens during aerobic biological treatment of sewage effluent?
questions.modelAnswer: Aerobic microorganisms break down/digest organic matter in the presence of oxygen.
markingPoints: Aerobic microorganisms break down/digest organic matter in the presence of oxygen.

questions.question: What happens to sewage sludge during anaerobic digestion?
questions.modelAnswer: Anaerobic microorganisms digest it without oxygen, producing biogas and treated sludge.
markingPoints: Anaerobic microorganisms digest it without oxygen, producing biogas and treated sludge.

questions.question: What is a low-grade ore?
questions.modelAnswer: An ore containing a small percentage/concentration of the desired metal compound.
markingPoints: An ore containing a small percentage/concentration of the desired metal compound.

questions.question: How does phytomining produce a metal-rich material?
questions.modelAnswer: Plants absorb metal ions from soil; plants are harvested and burned; the ash contains a higher concentration of metal compounds.
markingPoints: Plants absorb metal ions from soil
plants are harvested and burned
the ash contains a higher concentration of metal compounds.

questions.question: How does bioleaching extract metals from low-grade ores?
questions.modelAnswer: Bacteria convert metal compounds into soluble metal ions, producing a leachate from which the metal can be recovered.
markingPoints: Bacteria convert metal compounds into soluble metal ions, producing a leachate from which the metal can be recovered.

questions.question: State the four stages considered in a life-cycle assessment.
questions.modelAnswer: Raw-material extraction and processing; manufacture/packaging; use; end-of-life disposal, reuse or recycling.
markingPoints: Raw-material extraction and processing
manufacture/packaging
use
end-of-life disposal, reuse or recycling.

questions.question: Why can life-cycle assessments contain subjective judgements?
questions.modelAnswer: Environmental impacts may be difficult to quantify and different analysts may choose different boundaries or weight impacts differently.
markingPoints: Environmental impacts may be difficult to quantify and different analysts may choose different boundaries or weight impacts differently.

questions.question: Why does recycling metals usually save energy compared with extracting metals from ores?
questions.modelAnswer: Extraction and processing ores require mining and energy-intensive chemical processes; recycling avoids much of this.
markingPoints: Extraction and processing ores require mining and energy-intensive chemical processes
recycling avoids much of this.

questions.question: State the two conditions required for iron to rust.
questions.modelAnswer: Both oxygen and water must be present.
markingPoints: Both oxygen and water must be present.

questions.question: How does galvanising protect iron?
questions.modelAnswer: A zinc coating forms a barrier; if scratched, the more reactive zinc oxidises preferentially and provides sacrificial protection.
markingPoints: A zinc coating forms a barrier
if scratched, the more reactive zinc oxidises preferentially and provides sacrificial protection.

questions.question: Why are composites useful engineering materials?
questions.modelAnswer: They combine a matrix/binder with a reinforcement, giving useful properties from both, such as high strength with low mass.
markingPoints: They combine a matrix/binder with a reinforcement, giving useful properties from both, such as high strength with low mass.

questions.question: Compare producing potable water from fresh water and seawater.
questions.modelAnswer: Fresh water: choose source, filter and sterilise; generally lower energy/cost but supply may be limited/contaminated. Seawater desalination by distillation or reverse osmosis supplies arid areas but uses much energy, costs more and creates concentrated brine impacts.
markingPoints: Fresh water: choose source, filter and sterilise

generally lower energy/cost but supply may be limited/contaminated. Seawater desalination by distillation or reverse osmosis supplies arid areas but uses much energy, costs more and creates concentrated brine impacts.

questions.question: Evaluate paper and reusable plastic bags using a life-cycle assessment.
questions.modelAnswer: Compare raw materials, manufacture energy/water, transport mass, number of reuses, disposal/recycling and pollution. Paper may be renewable/biodegradable but can use more energy/water; plastic is durable/light but fossil-based and persistent. Conclusion depends on reuse and system boundaries/data.
markingPoints: Compare raw materials, manufacture energy/water, transport mass, number of reuses, disposal/recycling and pollution. Paper may be renewable/biodegradable but can use more energy/water
plastic is durable/light but fossil-based and persistent. Conclusion depends on reuse and system boundaries/data.

questions.question: Explain sacrificial protection of iron using zinc, including electron transfer.
questions.modelAnswer: Zinc is more reactive and oxidises preferentially: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. Electrons supplied to iron prevent iron atoms oxidising, so iron does not rust even if coating is scratched, while zinc is consumed.
markingPoints: Zinc is more reactive and oxidises preferentially: Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻. Electrons supplied to iron prevent iron atoms oxidising, so iron does not rust even if coating is scratched, while zinc is consumed.

questions.question: Compare a ceramic, a polymer and a composite for a bicycle component.
questions.modelAnswer: Ceramic is hard/heat resistant but brittle; polymer is light, corrosion-resistant and formable but may soften/creep; composite combines reinforcement and matrix for high strength-to-mass but may cost more and be difficult to recycle. Choice must match component forces and conditions.
markingPoints: Ceramic is hard/heat resistant but brittle
polymer is light, corrosion-resistant and formable but may soften/creep
composite combines reinforcement and matrix for high strength-to-mass but may cost more and be difficult to recycle. Choice must match component forces and conditions.

questions.question: Explain why recycling metals can reduce environmental impact but is not impact-free.
questions.modelAnswer: It reduces mining, finite-resource use, waste and often energy demand/emissions. However collection, transport, sorting, cleaning and remelting use energy; contamination can reduce quality, and some material is lost.
markingPoints: It reduces mining, finite-resource use, waste and often energy demand/emissions. However collection, transport, sorting, cleaning and remelting use energy
contamination can reduce quality, and some material is lost.

questions.question: Describe the laboratory production of potable water from a sample containing insoluble solids and dissolved salts.
questions.modelAnswer: Filter to remove insoluble solids; distil by boiling and condensing water to separate dissolved salts; collect distillate; test pH or dissolved solids as appropriate. Potable means safe to drink, not chemically pure.

questions.question: Explain why filtration alone cannot remove dissolved salts from water.
questions.modelAnswer: Dissolved ions/particles are much smaller than filter-paper pores and pass through with water. Distillation or another desalination method is required.
markingPoints: Dissolved ions/particles are much smaller than filter-paper pores and pass through with water. Distillation or another desalination method is required.

questions.question: Describe how to investigate the conditions needed for iron to rust.
questions.modelAnswer: Use cleaned identical iron nails in sealed tubes: dry air with a drying agent, boiled water with oil to exclude oxygen, and water plus air; keep time and temperature constant; compare rust; include repeats. Rust requires both oxygen and water.

questions.question: Explain why a life-cycle assessment conclusion depends on system boundaries and weighting.
questions.modelAnswer: Including or excluding extraction, manufacture, transport, use and disposal changes totals. Different impacts use different units and value judgements are needed to weight carbon, water, toxicity and waste, so assumptions must be stated and sensitivity considered.
markingPoints: Including or excluding extraction, manufacture, transport, use and disposal changes totals. Different impacts use different units and value judgements are needed to weight carbon, water, toxicity and waste, so assumptions must be stated and sensitivity considered.

questions.question: Evaluate whether recycled aluminium is always environmentally preferable to newly extracted aluminium.
questions.modelAnswer: Recycling usually saves energy and ore and reduces landfill, but collection, sorting, transport and contamination use resources. The conclusion depends on transport distances, energy source, recovery rate and product quality; compare quantified life-cycle data.
markingPoints: Recycling usually saves energy and ore and reduces landfill, but collection, sorting, transport and contamination use resources. The conclusion depends on transport distances, energy source, recovery rate and product quality
